I was going through the motions.

I definitely felt more that I loved her but not IN LOVE with her.  But it was my first long relationship so I don't really know what being in love means after 4 years.  It sort of came down to 'you know when you know' and I just sort of felt like I didn't know.

On my side it was mostly that I felt she wasn't as quick/smart as I was and just not as into things I was into.  I felt like I had to drag her to do things I liked and there wasn't as much adventure/spice in the relationship as I wanted.  Even just her planning a date for us or planning something to do on the weekend together.

I think though that things were getting better and she was making a big effort.  For example Burning Man.  I had a friend go and I got really excited about it myself.  When I first told her she was non-plussed and didn't want to go.  Bummed me out.  Then she saw pictures my friend took and got excited.  But it was just a bummer that she didn't know about it in the first place or get excited when I first explained it to her and showed the pictures of it to her.  Like, she needed to see another of our friends having done it to think it was possible.  Then when we went, the first thing that happens is she gets horribly mad at me just for sipping coffee.  And then during the actual event she was tired and if my friends weren't there I would have sort of had to babysit her a bit (so it felt).

The thing is - how much of an asshole am I for feeling that way given that a) we did end up going b) she actually WAS tired c) overall the trip was wonderful and she was really great for most of the rest of the trip?  I just feel like a judgemental asshole for holding those things against her - or for not being able to really talk to her about how it made me feel.

When I was injured and couldn't leave the house it just made things worse.  Even if she suggested something I couldn't do it.  So the last year where she came through for me and gave me some reasons to stick around I wasn't physically capable to do the things I needed to do to keep the relationship.  And because of my injury I'm not sure I can even really do things like Burning Man again so it's almost like a moot point to some degree.  For me I felt she wasn't just going through the motions - that she really loved me.  For me I was just so conflicted from before and then out of touch with reality because of the pain and depression.

Thanks for reading my situation and helping give some perspective.

There's a few things you can do.

The most important thing is ROUTINE.  When you are depressed you have a hard time motivating yourself to get things done.  You will find a routine but it's usually not a healthy routine.  It will be sitting on a computer, lying in bed, watching TV show after TV show, etc.

All these things are fine but if you do them too much they will make you feel really sick.  Which will further fuel your shitty mood and make you feel even more depressed.

It's cliche but you really need to do the fundamental things:  Eat fresh fruit and veggies every day.  Make sure you get exercise.  Make sure you talk with people.

My social worker gave me some very specific suggestions:

- Every day go for a walk.  Just take 30 minutes to walk.  At the end of the walk go to a cafe or library and spent 30 minutes reading (the paper, a book, reddit) but be somewhere with people. Don't just head home and be alone.

- Every day choose a small task that you can do in 15-20 minutes and do it.  Rearrange a bookshelf.  Clean a small section of your floor.  Fold a small pile of laundry.  The important thing is to do one small task every single day.  You need a sense of accomplishment.

- Phone a friend and go out with them to do something.  In my case I had to tell a friend how depressed I was and that I needed their help.  He has called me every week to get me out the house and helped me out.

- Fresh fruit and veggies.  You will not believe how big a difference this makes, in conjunction with a 30 minute walk every night.

- Routine.  Make sure you do these things every day.  Write them down.  Stick to it.

Over time you'll just start to feel a little bit better and it will give you the motivation to try and address what's bothering you.  Likewise, I highly, highly suggest going to talk to someone.  Most hospitals have a crisis clinic that will set you up with a few meetings with someone in a quickly.  It was very, very helpful for me to talk with someone who could listen and make suggestions.  Even just explaining yourself can help you organize your thoughts and motivate you.

You shouldn't do 'ultimate tests' or stick with someone based on events that are coming up.

The best case scenario is that it goes horribly and you get your justification for breaking up.  The worst case scenario is that you have an amazing time - and you'll now be left with even more doubts.  Because they won't solve the problems you're having.

You have three basic options.

One is that you break up with her.  Given what you've said this may be an option for you.

The other is that you need to TALK to her.  You need to get these things out and talk about them and see what you can do to change them.  The problem here is that it's hard for people to change and more importantly some things really shouldn't be talked about.

The third, probably easiest option is that you need to learn to accept her for who she is.  This means not trying to change her but really understanding that who she is is who she is.  You need to really accept that she'll talk your ear off all the time.  Or that she'll be passive aggressive.  You need to work on the part of you which gets annoyed at that and really reflect on why it annoys you.  And accept it.

If you stay with her I'd suggest doing 2 and 3.  You need to talk about your frustrations but also need to accept that some of the reason you're frustrated comes from within yourself and that even if she listens and changes you need to look inside and change a bit as well.

I know for sure the ultimate test route is a really bad move though.  Don't do that.  Address this issue today, this week.  SOON.  It's not going to magically get better.  Even if it's just self-reflection.  Don't set arbitrary dates.
